topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's scope and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how clonal succession, Darwinian natural selection, and epigenetic alterations drive the acquisition of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell models in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of tissue hierarchy, stemness properties, and specific cells of origin in initiating and propagating tumors.

topics.label: Role of the microenvironment, inflammation, and stroma in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how chronic inflammation, microenvironmental signaling, and stromal dependencies promote cancer initiation, progression, and therapeutic targeting.

topics.label: Methods for studying tumor evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the experimental, sequencing, and computational methods used to analyze clonal evolution and spatial interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin properties, and permissive microenvironments within an evolutionary framework.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
